focus: weighted interpolation, factorization, ramification cleanup, and characteristic-safe propagation

messages.body_markdown: The minimal round-2 handoff no longer needs an inherited minimum-degree core. Please return a rank-reaching certificate $(G,R,D)$ with $e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$, $D\le K_\theta d$, and more than $D$ reached accepted points on every target line. AE-16 then performs global cleanup and degree-$D$ peeling.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight handoff replaces core handoff

messages.body_markdown: AE-19 isolates the safe factor-linearization statement with $\Delta\le D<p$, not $\Delta<D$. The common lift must satisfy $C_Z\ne0$: researcher-0006 P7--P9 gives a minimum-weight singular counterexample without this hypothesis. At a simple lift, formal implicit uniqueness and more than $\Delta$ directions yield $C=u(Z-Q)$.
messages.subject: Simple-lift factor linearization

messages.body_markdown: The Vinh-free aggregation is AE-20: once $C=u(Z-Q)$, every point in the entire factor class satisfies $Q=f$, including across disconnected components, and point density is at least normalized class-edge mass. Please correct E2E-22 from $\Delta<D$ to $\Delta\le D<p$.
messages.subject: Corrected global factor aggregation

messages.body_markdown: The researcher-0007 factorwise polar audit is no longer pending: P1--P5 were judged mathematically sound, but the enclosing verdict remains revise because of auxiliary wording and a literature citation. AE-10 therefore records the result as a candidate fallback. The bounded-weight critical path instead uses whole-relation cleanup in AE-16; assigned-factor differentiation remains important if that interface is weakened.
messages.subject: Factorwise polar audit update

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence instance
nodes.notes: This fixes the campaign regime $m=2$ and excludes both dimension bootstrapping and $d\le100$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and polynomials $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for every affine line $L$. Let $$\mathcal I=\{(x,L):x\in L\text{ and }P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ For $E\subseteq\mathcal I$, define $e(E)=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$.

nodes.label: Weighted restriction map
nodes.notes: This is the Lean-level linear map whose joint rank must be controlled.
nodes.statement_markdown: Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$ and put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}(A)\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2}.$$ For an affine parametrization $L(t)$, set $\rho_L(A)=A(L(t),P_L(t))$. For $R$ a line family, define $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\longrightarrow\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\longmapsto(\rho_M(A))_{M\in R}.$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching certificate
nodes.notes: Unlike the round-1 core interface, this certificate carries mass and reach but need not initially have minimum degree.
nodes.statement_markdown: A rank-reaching certificate is $(G,R,D)$ where $G=(X,T,E)$ is an accepted subgraph, $R\subseteq T$, $d\le D$, $|R|>D$, and $$\operatorname{rank}(\Phi_{R,D})<\dim V_D.$$ Moreover, every $L\in T$ satisfies $$\left|\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\}\right|>D.$$ Write $e(G)=e(E)$.

nodes.label: Constant-loss core pruning
nodes.notes: This remains an off-path interface: the source step is individually exact, but its enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $e(\mathcal I)=\epsilon$, there is an accepted subgraph of mass at least $\epsilon/4$ and minimum degree at least $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$.

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: This preserves the exact accepted component-level backbone from round 1.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G$ be a connected accepted subgraph of minimum degree $k$, let $t$ be its number of lines, and put $\tau=t/[p(p+1)]$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Whole-explainer square-root floor
nodes.notes: This is an architectural ceiling, not an impossibility theorem for rank-aware interpolation.
nodes.statement_markdown: The AE-05 construction has $$|R|=\Theta\left(\frac{\tau p^2}{k}\right),\qquad D=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{d\tau p^2}{k}}\right),\qquad D<k.$$ Together with $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, this forces $k^2=\Omega(dp)$ and hence cannot reach $k=\Theta(\epsilon p)$ below $\epsilon=\Omega((d/p)^{1/2})$.

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The direct-decoder alternative in AE-12 is essential.
nodes.statement_markdown: For suitable legal instances with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$, every line family reaching half the accepted points of every accepted line has size at least $p/(32\epsilon)$, although a constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Uniform-jet rank barrier
nodes.notes: This is diagnostic only: the source audit requires integer parameters and restricts the claim to the raw-feasible regime.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $s,D\in\mathbb Z$ with $s\ge1$, $d\le D<p$, and $n>D$. Define $$C_s(D,d)=\sum_{a+b<s}\max(D-a-db+1,0).$$ If raw dimension counting gives $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$ and transfer uses $h$ compatible intersections with $sh>D$, then $$h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.$$

nodes.label: Characteristic-safe separability and resultants
nodes.notes: The exact condition is $B_Z\ne0$; the degree bound is a sufficient characteristic-safe criterion, not a necessary one.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $B$ is squarefree and primitive in $Z$ with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(B)<pd$, then $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. If coprime $U,V$ have weighted degrees $u,v$ and $Z$-degrees $r,s$, respectively, then the number of graph lines on which both vanish identically is at most $$su+rv-drs.$$

nodes.label: Assigned-factor polar cleanup
nodes.notes: The source audit was exact and judged P1--P5 mathematically sound, but its enclosing verdict is revise. This is an auxiliary fallback, not part of the bounded-weight critical path.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $B=c\prod_iC_i$ be primitive and squarefree with $\operatorname{wdeg}(B)<p$, and assign each graph line to one factor. Put $$\delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i),\quad r_i=\deg_Z(C_i),\quad\gamma_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_{i,Z}),$$ and $$\Xi_i=(r_i-1)\delta_i+r_i\gamma_i-dr_i(r_i-1).$$ If $T_i$ is the assigned line class and $b_i$ is its number of identically ramified lines, then $$b_i\le\min\{|T_i|,\Xi_i\},\qquad\gamma_i\le\delta_i-d,\qquad\Xi_i\le\frac{\delta_i^2}{d}-\delta_i.$$ The ramified accepted incidences satisfy $$\frac{|E_{\mathrm{ram}}|}{p^2(p+1)}\le\sum_i\frac{\min\{|T_i|,\Xi_i\}}{p(p+1)}+\sum_i\frac{|T_i|\gamma_i}{p^2(p+1)}.$$

nodes.label: Singular-seed obstruction
nodes.notes: This prevents silently dropping the simple-root hypothesis from AE-19.
nodes.statement_markdown: For legal choices with $d+1<p$, there is a primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible polynomial $$C=XZ+H(Y),\qquad\operatorname{wdeg}(C)=d+1,$$ supporting more than $d+1$ compatible degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines through one common lift, but no $Q$ of total degree at most $d$ with $C(X,Y,Q)=0$. At the common lift, $C_Z=0$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal open campaign lemma. AE-07 rules out a graph-only proof without the decoder branch.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there are constants $C_\theta,a_\theta>0$ and $K_\theta\ge1$ such that, whenever $$e(\mathcal I)=\epsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta},$$ either one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $\Pr[Q=f]\ge a_\theta\epsilon$, or there is a rank-reaching certificate $(G,R,D)$ with $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter gate
nodes.notes: This is where the strict $D=O_\theta(d)$ interface removes the round-1 unbounded-factor gap.
nodes.statement_markdown: After increasing $C_\theta$ in AE-12, the relation alternative satisfies $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\left(\frac dp\right)^\theta\le\frac{a_\theta}{100}.$$ Consequently, $$D<p,\qquad \left(\frac Dp\right)^2+\frac{3D}{p}\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2}.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: The radicalization argument preserves every selected graph identity because each restriction ring is an integral domain.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation alternative, there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ with $$\rho_M(A)=0\quad(M\in R),\qquad A_Z\ne0.$$ Indeed, take a nonzero kernel element and replace it by the product of its distinct irreducible factors. The inequality $|R|>D$ excludes a $Z$-independent relation, while $\deg_Z(A)\le D/d<p$ makes $Z$-dependence characteristic-safe.

nodes.label: Reached-root identity extension
nodes.notes: Distinct reached points give distinct roots of the target restriction.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line $L$ of $G$, $$\rho_L(A)=A(L(t),P_L(t))=0.$$ Each reached accepted point is a root of $\rho_L(A)$ because it also lies on a selected line $M\in R$ and both labels equal $f$ there. Since $\deg\rho_L(A)\le D$, more than $D$ such roots force the identity.

nodes.label: Global characteristic-safe cleanup
nodes.notes: The accepted source supplies the local cleanup and simplicity arguments; their global normalized-mass assembly is the new drafting task.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient gcd in $Z$. Delete content lines and the degeneracies of a formal directional derivative coprime to $B$; this removes at most $pD^2+D|T|$ accepted edges. Then repeatedly delete vertices of current degree at most $D$. The surviving graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ satisfies $$e(G_1)\ge a_\theta\epsilon-\left(\frac Dp\right)^2-\frac{3D}{p}\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2},\qquad \min_{v\in X_1\sqcup T_1}\deg_{G_1}(v)>D.$$ Moreover, $$B(L(t),P_L(t))=0\quad(L\in T_1),\qquad B(x,f(x))=0,\quad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0\quad(x\in X_1).$$

nodes.label: Simple-root factor-pure partition
nodes.notes: This replaces the round-1 heavy-factor-or-cross-factor obligation when $D/d$ is bounded.
nodes.statement_markdown: Factor the primitive squarefree relation as $B=c\prod_{i=1}^sC_i$ over $\mathbb F_p$. Every $C_i$ depends on $Z$, so $$s\le\frac{\operatorname{wdeg}(B)}d\le\frac Dd\le K_\theta.$$ At every point of $G_1$, exactly one factor vanishes because $B_Z\ne0$. Every line has exactly one identically vanishing factor, and an edge joins a line and point carrying the same factor. Thus $G_1$ is the disjoint union of factor-pure classes, and every vertex retains its full $G_1$-degree inside its class.

nodes.label: Constant-factor concentration
nodes.notes: No resultant or incidence mixing is needed after the factor-pure partition.
nodes.statement_markdown: Some factor $C_i$ with $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i)$ has a class $G_i=(X_i,T_i,E_i)$ satisfying $$e(E_i)\ge\frac{e(G_1)}s\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta},\qquad \min_{v\in X_i\sqcup T_i}\deg_{G_i}(v)>D\ge\Delta_i.$$

nodes.label: Simple-seed factor linearization
nodes.notes: Translate the seed to the origin, construct the unique formal implicit root by dividing only by the nonzero scalar $C_Z$, kill homogeneous terms of degrees $d<j\le\Delta$ using more than $\Delta$ projective directions and $\Delta<p$, and then use the kernel $(Z-Q)$ of substitution. A fresh standalone proof is still required because the closest factorwise source has verdict revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible and $Z$-dependent with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(C)\le D<p$. Suppose $C(b,\alpha)=0$, $C_Z(b,\alpha)\ne0$, and more than $\Delta$ distinct affine lines through $b$ carry polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d$ such that $$P_L(b)=\alpha,\qquad C(L(t),P_L(t))=0.$$ Then there are $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ and $u\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ such that $$C=u(Z-Q).$$ Applied to AE-18, this linearizes $C_i$.

nodes.label: Disconnected factor aggregation
nodes.notes: This is the Vinh-free list-to-single-polynomial handoff.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C_i=u(Z-Q)$ be the factor from AE-19. Every $x\in X_i$ satisfies $Q(x)=f(x)$, including points in different connected components. Since each point lies on at most $p+1$ affine lines, $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{|X_i|}{p^2}\ge\frac{|E_i|}{p^2(p+1)}=e(E_i)\ge\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional fixed-theta algebraic engine
nodes.notes: The direct branch comes from AE-12; the relation branch is AE-13--AE-20.
nodes.statement_markdown: Assuming AE-12 and AE-19, for every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there are $C_\theta,c_\theta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr[Q=f]\ge c_\theta\epsilon,$$ where one may take $c_\theta=a_\theta/(2K_\theta)$.

nodes.label: Near-linear algebraic propagation engine
nodes.notes: No corpus submission proves the bounded-weight dichotomy. The endpoint remains blocked on AE-12 and the standalone formalization of AE-16 and AE-19.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\eta<1$, there are constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every accepted-incidence instance of density $\epsilon$, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

summary: Round 2 replaces the weaker relation bound $D\le A_\eta d\epsilon^{-\eta/(1-\eta)}$ by the strict bounded-weight rank-or-decode interface $D\le K_\theta d$. That change makes the irreducible-factor count $s\le D/d$ constant, so the former heavy-factor-versus-cross-factor gap collapses to pigeonhole concentration. The critical relation branch is: extract a squarefree rank-kernel relation, extend it by reached roots, perform characteristic-safe whole-relation cleanup, globally peel to minimum degree greater than $D$, partition into simple factor-pure classes, linearize one factor at a simple high-direction seed, and aggregate its disconnected class without Vinh mixing. The accepted component decoder and selector obstruction are retained off-path; the exact-revise factorwise polar theorem is retained as a fallback. Accepted singular examples show that $C_Z\ne0$ at the seed is indispensable. The main unresolved input is AE-12, with AE-16 and AE-19 still requiring standalone formalization.
target_statement: Prove an algebraic interpolation-and-propagation lemma strong enough to preserve a near-linear power of the accepted incidence density over $\mathbb F_p^2$.
title: Algebraic propagation engine
